findings_to_judge.finding: Canaan's self-mining run-rate halved entering Q3 while it reported installed hashrate as flat: monthly BTC produced went 90 (April) / 90 (May) / 64 (June) / 46 (July) = 3.00 / 2.90 / 2.13 / 1.48 BTC per day, a 51% per-day decline, driven by Ethiopia (4.96 EH/s, a third of the 14.9 EH/s installed fleet) falling from 2.33 EH/s operating at 30 April to 0.36 EH/s at 30 June and then being described as 'paused' at 31 July -- yet the July release counted the entire paused 4.96 EH/s inside its headline 'operating computing power' of 14.24 EH/s, one month after the same table had shown Ethiopia at 0.36 EH/s operating.

Canaan converted its automatic shelf into a $270m standard Form F-3 on 15 April 2026 specifically because it 'expects that it will cease to be a well-known seasoned issuer' on filing its FY2025 20-F, then filed Post-Effective Amendment No. 5 on 15 June 2026 as an 'exhibits-only filing to file an updated auditor consent' -- i.e. it is actively keeping a shelf equal to roughly its entire market value usable -- against cash that fell from US$80.8m at 31 December 2025 to US$43.5m at 31 March 2026, a Q1 gross LOSS of US$22.9m, US$21.1m short-term debt, and zero 424B5 takedowns anywhere in 2026 after three in 2025 (March, October, November).

There is a mid-June 2026 open-market insider buy cluster that is essentially invisible for this name because Canaan is a 20-F/6-K filer whose officers nonetheless file Section 16 forms: CFO Cheng Jin bought 65,000 ADSs at US$0.35 on 15 June, and CEO Nangeng Zhang bought 250,000 ADSs at US$0.34 on 17 June and 250,000 at US$0.33 on 18 June, and no insider has filed any transaction since 22 June -- no sales at all into the 68% rally.

Canaan is inside its second and final Nasdaq minimum-bid-price compliance period, expiring 11 January 2027, with the ADSs at US$0.36 -- needing roughly +178% and then ten consecutive closes at or above US$1.00 -- and the company has committed to nothing more than that it 'will evaluate all available options during the second compliance period to rectify the deficiency'; I found no depositary notice of any Canaan reverse split or ADS-ratio change, and an ADS-ratio change (currently 1 ADS = 15 Class A shares) needs no shareholder vote and can be effected in weeks.

Cipher Mining's 53,762,660 CAN ADSs (806,439,900 Class A shares, ~9.2% of the 585.8m reported float), issued to it at US$0.7394/ADS on 2026-02-23 as payment for the ABC Projects JV stake, came out of lock-up on 2026-08-23 -- Cipher's own 10-Q states the date and carries the position inside 'Prepaid expenses and other current assets', and the shares were never registered for resale, so Cipher can sell under Rule 144 as a non-affiliate with no volume cap and no Form 144 trail.

The 2026-08-04 'repurchase shares using digital asset treasury' release that lit the +68% run adds no new authorisation and no dollar figure -- it points back to a US$30m board authorisation dated 2025-12-12 that expires 2026-12-12 and that Canaan's own Q1 release says had bought only ~2.8m ADSs for ~US$2.0m (6.7%), after the prior US$30m programme executed just US$4.9m (16%); the Sept 8 release is the first document that must state repurchases through 30 June.
